claim: The Data Layer's core-metrics-extractor plugin selects per-pod metric specs via an engineConfigs list keyed by a Kubernetes Pod label (default key inference.networking.k8s.io/engine-type, default engine 'vllm' for unlabeled pods), mapping engine name to PromQL-style spec strings for queue depth, running requests, KV-cache usage, LoRA info, and cache config -- this label-driven dispatch is the concrete mechanism that would need generalizing for non-pod backends.
stance_target: locating exactly where pod-label-based engine detection lives in the metrics extraction path
scope_conditions: GIE EndpointPickerConfig, pre-June-2026 version (moved into llm-d-router afterward)
quoted_support: Pod label used to select which engineConfig to apply. Default: "inference.networking.k8s.io/engine-type" ... Engine to use for Pods without the engineLabelKey label. Must match a name in engineConfigs. Default: "vllm"

claim: The built-in metrics-data-source plugin scrapes metrics over plain HTTP(S) directly to each endpoint's own address (scheme http/https, default path /metrics, insecureSkipVerify true by default) -- i.e. the scraping mechanism itself is address-agnostic and does not hard-code 'pod IP' anywhere in its parameter schema, so any address string the Data Layer resolves for an endpoint would work.
stance_target: claim that k8s-pod-IP scraping is architecturally unavoidable in the metrics-data-source plugin itself
quoted_support:
parameters:
  scheme: "http"    # or "https". Default: "http"
  path: "/metrics"  # Default: "/metrics"
  insecureSkipVerify: true  # Default: true

claim: An explicit empty data.sources: [] is valid and silently disables all metric collection (with a warning), which is distinct from omitting the data section or setting it null, which is a hard startup error only when the dataLayer feature gate is enabled -- relevant to how a custom backend could legally opt out of the built-in k8s-oriented DataSource wiring.
stance_target: legal ways to disable the default k8s-pod metrics DataSource without breaking startup
quoted_support: omitted / null, datalayer enabled (dataLayer feature gate) | startup error: "You must specify the Data section" ... sources: [] (empty list) | warning logged, no collection

claim: The EndpointPickerConfig explicitly documents that although its YAML resembles a Kubernetes CRD, it is NOT a CRD -- it is not reconciled, only read once at EPP process startup, an intentional design so scheduling config can't drift without a redeploy.
stance_target: clarifying the config's relationship (or non-relationship) to the Kubernetes control plane
quoted_support: While the configuration text looks like a Kubernetes CRD, it is NOT a Kubernetes CRD. Specifically, the config is not reconciled upon, and is only read on startup. This behavior is intentional

claim: SGLang engine metric defaults are auto-selected when a Pod carries the inference.networking.k8s.io/engine-type: sglang label, demonstrating the built-in extractor already ships multi-engine support gated purely on a label value rather than on hard-coded engine detection logic.
stance_target: existence of a working multi-backend-type precedent inside the stock metrics extractor
quoted_support: SGLang defaults are also built in and selected automatically when a Pod carries the inference.networking.k8s.io/engine-type: sglang label.
